mainTopic: When a מודעא is valid, the hidden gift (מתנתא טמירתא), and whether a hidden gift cancels another gift
overview: This amud finishes a rule about the wording of a מודעא: the witnesses must write that they know about the person's duress. The גמרא asks what kind of deal this rule is about. A גט or a מתנה needs no proof of pressure, and רבא said we don't write a מודעא for a sale. The answer is that it is about a sale where the seller was truly forced, like the orchard story. Next, רב יהודה rules that a hidden gift document cannot be used to collect, and רב יוסף defines a hidden gift in two versions that differ when the giver said nothing. רבא is quoted as saying a hidden gift also cancels another gift. רב פפא shows this was only inferred from a story about a woman and an eldest son. In that story the woman's gift really failed because it was given under obvious pressure. The amud ends by opening a new question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A declaration must mention the known duress
steps.stepSummary: A מודעא that does not say 'we know of so-and-so's duress' is not a valid מודעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A declaration that does not have written in it, 'We know about the duress of so-and-so,' is not a valid declaration.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a rule that began just before this section: a מודעא only works if the witnesses write that they know the person is being forced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מודעא is a quiet statement before witnesses: 'What I am about to do, I am doing against my will.' This rule adds a requirement. The witnesses must confirm they actually know about the pressure. Just saying 'I don't really mean it' is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A protest declaration made before witnesses, saying a coming act is done under pressure

phrases.english: That does not have written in it:
phrases.notes: The 'that' here is the מודעא, which comes up just before this section starts.

phrases.english: "We know about him
the duress of so-and-so"
is not a declaration.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָא כְּתִיב בָּהּ אֲנַן יָדְעִינַן בֵּיהּ בְּאוּנְסָא דִפְלָנְיָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מודעא is valid only if it states that the witnesses know of the person's duress.

steps.title: Which kind of deal is this rule about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of מודעא needs this wording. A גט or a מתנה cannot be meant, because there a simple statement is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: A declaration for what? If it is for a bill of divorce or a gift, that is merely revealing the matter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which kind of deal this rule is talking about, and rules out a גט or a מתנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט and a מתנה only happen if the person really wants them. So if he reveals that he doesn't want it, that alone cancels it, and he doesn't need to prove any duress. The strict wording requirement therefore can't be about these cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Merely revealing what one really thinks

phrases.english: A declaration for what?
If it is for a bill of divorce or a gift,
it is merely revealing the matter!
phrases.notes: He means that here, just showing he doesn't want it is enough. No proof of pressure is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what case the rule in step 1 applies to
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of transaction requires the 'we know of his duress' wording?

steps.title: But רבא said no declaration for a sale
steps.stepSummary: The rule can't be about a sale either, because רבא said we do not write a מודעא for a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is for a sale — but didn't רבא say: We do not write a declaration for a sale!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other option, a sale, and attacks it with a statement of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a גט and a מתנה ruled out, a sale is the remaining option. But רבא said a מודעא is not written for a sale at all. So it seems there is no case left for the rule in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: And if it is for a sale,
but didn't רבא say:
We do not write a declaration for a sale!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off the second possible case, so no case seems to remain
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in step 1 requiring special wording in a מודעא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט or מתנה doesn't need it, and רבא says a sale gets no מודעא at all, so the rule has no case to apply to.

steps.title: It is a sale where the seller was truly forced
steps.stepSummary: The rule really is about a sale. רבא agrees that a מודעא is written when the seller is actually forced, like in the orchard story.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is about a sale. רבא agrees where the person was forced, like the incident of the orchard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule is about a sale. רבא's rule doesn't cover a case of real pressure, and the גמרא is about to tell a story to show such a case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule covers an ordinary sale, where the seller chose to sell, often because he needed the money. When someone is truly being forced into the sale, רבא agrees a מודעא is written. That explains why the witnesses must state they know of the duress.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (keeps the original option and defends it)

phrases.english: Actually, it is about a sale;
רבא agrees where he was forced,
like the incident of the orchard;

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם דִּזְבִינֵי מוֹדֵי רָבָא הֵיכָא דַּאֲנִיס
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of רבא's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's rule seemed to block every מודעא for any sale.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא only means an ordinary sale. When the seller is really forced, a מודעא is written.

steps.title: The orchard story: when we do write a declaration
steps.stepSummary: A man held an orchard as a pledge for three years, long enough to claim חזקה. He then threatened to hide the pledge document and say he bought it unless the owner sold it to him. In a case like this, a מודעא is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man pledged an orchard to his friend for three years. After the lender used it for the three years of חזקה, he said: 'If you sell it to me, good. If not, I will hide the pledge document and say, "It was bought, and that is why it is in my hands."' In a case like this we write a declaration.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the orchard story to show what real pressure on a seller looks like, and concludes that in such a case a מודעא is written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After three years of using land, a person can claim he bought it (חזקה). The lender could hide the שטר משכנתא, and the owner would lose the orchard completely. The owner is pushed into selling against his will, so his מודעא protects him.

keyTerms.meaning: Pledged (gave the land as security for a loan)
Three years of use that lets a holder claim ownership

steps.whatToRemember: A מודעא is not written for an ordinary sale, but it is written when the seller is truly forced, like the orchard owner threatened with losing everything.

phrases.english: For a certain man pledged an orchard
to his friend for three years.
After he used it for the three years of חזקה,
phrases.notes: Literally 'ate it,' meaning he enjoyed its fruit. The one doing this is the lender holding the orchard.

phrases.english: he said: If you sell it to me, good;
and if not, I will hide the pledge document,
and I will say: "It is bought, in my hands."
In a case like this, we write a declaration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the story mentioned in step 4 and states the result
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When a seller is truly forced, as in the orchard case, a מודעא is written even for a sale.

steps.title: A hidden gift document cannot collect
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a document for a hidden gift cannot be used to collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: With this hidden gift, we do not collect with it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב יהודה rules that a gift written in secret is not enforced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The recipient holding a document of a hidden gift cannot use it in בית דין to take the property. The גמרא does not explain the reason here. It first moves on to define what counts as 'hidden.'

phrases.english: רב יהודה said:
This hidden gift,
we do not collect with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה הַאי מַתַּנְתָּא טְמִירְתָּא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hidden-gift document cannot be used to collect.

steps.title: What counts as a hidden gift?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact case of a hidden gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of a hidden gift?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of רב יהודה's term. This sets up רב יוסף's answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the rule can be applied, we need to know which gifts count as 'hidden.'

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: What is the case of a hidden gift?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of a hidden gift

steps.title: רב יוסף: he told witnesses to hide
steps.stepSummary: In the first version, רב יוסף says a hidden gift is when the giver told the witnesses to go hide and write the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: When he told the witnesses, 'Go hide and write it for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the first definition: the giver openly asked for secrecy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this version, a gift is only 'hidden' if the giver actually told the witnesses to keep it secret.

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
When he said to the witnesses:
"Go hide and write it for him."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמַר לְהוּ לְסָהֲדִי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A hidden gift is when the giver told the witnesses to hide while writing it.

steps.title: Other version: he didn't tell them to write in public
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב יוסף says a gift is hidden unless the giver told the witnesses to sit in the market or outdoors and write it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב יוסף said: When he did not tell them, 'Sit in the market and outdoors and write it for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב יוסף's definition, which is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the gift counts as hidden unless the giver actually told the witnesses to write it in public. So the gift only works with a public instruction.

phrases.english: And some say: רב יוסף said:
When he did not say to them:
"Sit in the market and outdoors
and write it for him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב יוסף's definition
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A gift is hidden whenever the giver did not tell the witnesses to write it publicly.

steps.title: What is the difference between the versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two versions of רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the two versions of רב יוסף would give different results. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree on the clear cases, so the גמרא looks for the case that separates them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between the two versions

steps.title: The difference: when he said nothing
steps.stepSummary: The versions differ when the giver gave no instruction about secrecy or publicity.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is when he said nothing either way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the versions split when the giver said nothing about where to write it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the first version, the gift is hidden only if he said 'hide,' so a gift with no instruction is fine and can collect. By the second version, it is hidden unless he said 'write in public,' so a gift with no instruction counts as hidden and cannot collect.

keyTerms.meaning: Unspecified, with no instruction either way

steps.whatToRemember: A hidden gift can't collect. The two versions of רב יוסף disagree only when the giver gave no instruction: the first version allows that gift, the second treats it as hidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume both versions agree whenever there was no 'hide' instruction. In the second version, silence is enough to make the gift count as hidden.

phrases.english: The difference between them is an unspecified case.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ when the giver gave no instruction about secrecy or publicity.

steps.title: A hidden gift cancels a later gift
steps.stepSummary: רבא is quoted as ruling that a hidden gift acts as a מודעא that cancels a second gift of the same item.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And a hidden gift serves as a protest that cancels the other, later gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling in רבא's name. It says the hidden gift we just defined has a further effect: it cancels a later gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we only learned that a hidden gift itself cannot collect. Here רבא is quoted as adding something more. The hidden gift works like a מודעא: it shows that the giver does not truly want a later gift of the same thing to take effect. So the second recipient also gets nothing. The next steps question whether רבא really said this.

keyTerms.meaning: A declaration or protest that the giver is acting against his will, which cancels the act
For its fellow, meaning the other, later gift

phrases.english: Rava said:
And it serves as a protest for the other one.
phrases.notes: The 'it' is the hidden gift, and 'the other one' is a second gift of the same item made later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further legal effect to the hidden gift that was just defined
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hidden gift acts as a מודעא that cancels a later gift of the same property.

steps.title: רבא never said this outright
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the ruling credited to רבא was never said in words. People only inferred it from one of his rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This statement of רבא was not said explicitly; it was only inferred.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges whether רבא really said the ruling in step 12. He also sets up the story that shows where the idea came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא does not attack the logic head-on. He questions the source. If the ruling was only inferred, it may be a mistaken reading of what רבא meant, and the next steps show this.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, drawn out from something else

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This statement of Rava was not stated explicitly,
rather, it was stated by inference.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּרָבָא לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִיתְּמַר אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the ruling in step 12 really came from רבא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבא explicitly ruled that a hidden gift cancels a later gift
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling was only inferred from a case, not stated outright

steps.title: The story of the woman and the eldest son
steps.stepSummary: A man writes all his property to a woman because she demands it as a condition for marriage. When his eldest son complains, he secretly has witnesses write a document giving the property to the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man went to marry a woman. She said: If you write all your property to me, I will marry you; if not, I won't. He wrote it all to her. His eldest son came and said: And what will become of me? The father told witnesses: Go hide in עבר ימינא and write a gift document for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tells the case that the inference came from. Two gifts are made of the same property: an open one to the woman and a hidden one to the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two gifts of the same property are involved: an open one to the woman and a hidden one to the son. The father told the witnesses to hide, which matches רב יוסף's first definition of a hidden gift.

phrases.english: For a certain man went to betroth a woman;

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: ״אִי כָּתְבַתְּ לִי כּוּלְּהוּ נִכְסָיךְ –
phrases.english: she said to him: "If you write all of your property to me,
I will be yours,
and if not, I will not be yours."
He went and wrote all his property to her.
His eldest son came and said to him:
"And that man, what will become of him?"
phrases.notes: 'That man' is the son talking about himself, a polite way of saying 'me'.

phrases.english: He said to the witnesses:
"Go hide in Avar Yemina,
and write it for him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the case from which רבא's supposed ruling was inferred
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a case with an open gift to the woman followed by a hidden gift to the son

steps.title: רבא rules that neither one acquires
steps.stepSummary: The case comes before רבא, who rules that neither the son nor the woman acquires the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before רבא. He said to them: Neither this one acquired, nor that one acquired.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his ruling: both gifts fail. This ruling is what people used to build the inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son's gift fails because it was a hidden gift. The surprise is that the woman's open gift also fails, and רבא does not say why. That missing reason is what led people to guess.
steps.confusionAlert: Both 'מר's look the same, but one refers to the son and the other to the woman. Neither of them gets the property.

phrases.english: They came before Rava; he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: לָא מָר קְנָה, וְלָא מָר קְנָה.
phrases.english: This master did not acquire, and that master did not acquire.
phrases.notes: One 'master' is the son and the other is the woman; neither ends up owning the property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא, אֲמַר לְהוּ: לָא מָר קְנָה, וְלָא מָר קְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's ruling on the story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither the son (hidden gift) nor the woman acquires the property.

steps.title: Observers think the hidden gift canceled the woman's gift
steps.stepSummary: People who saw the ruling assumed the woman lost because the hidden gift worked as a מודעא against her gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever saw this assumed it was because a hidden gift serves as a protest canceling the other gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly how the mistaken inference was made. Observers explained the woman's loss with the rule from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבא did not explain why the woman lost, observers supplied a reason themselves. They said the hidden gift to the son revealed that the father never truly meant his gift to her. That guess became 'רבא's ruling' in step 12.

phrases.english: Whoever saw it thought:
it is because it serves as a protest for the other one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how observers drew step 12's rule from רבא's ruling
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a hidden gift cancels a later gift
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling that the woman did not acquire

steps.title: The real reason: her gift was forced
steps.stepSummary: The inference is wrong. The woman lost because it was clear the father wrote to her under pressure. In an ordinary case, the giver may truly want the public gift to stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There, it was obvious that he wrote it to her because of pressure. But here, in an ordinary case, maybe he wants this one to acquire and does not want that one to acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the observers' reasoning and gives the true reason for רבא's ruling. With that, the 'rule' in step 12 falls away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman's gift failed because she pressured him: no gift, no marriage. That pressure (אונס) was obvious. In a normal case nobody forced the giver. He may have hidden the first gift precisely because he did not want it to work and did want the public one to stand. So a hidden gift does not automatically cancel a later gift.

keyTerms.meaning: He is pleased, he wants it

steps.whatToRemember: A hidden gift by itself does not cancel a later gift. רבא canceled the woman's gift only because it clearly came from pressure.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that you cannot build a general rule from a ruling without knowing its real reason. A special detail (אונס) explained the case.

phrases.english: But it is not so;
there, the matter is evident
that it was because of pressure that he wrote it to her;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא – מָר נִיחָא לֵיהּ דְּלִיקְנֵי,
phrases.english: but here, he wants this master to acquire,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means an ordinary case of a hidden gift followed by a public one, with no pressure.

phrases.english: and he does not want that master to acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the observers' inference in step 16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that a hidden gift serves as a מודעא for a later gift
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The woman's gift failed because of obvious אונס, a detail missing from ordinary cases
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A hidden gift does not cancel a later public gift; רבא's ruling rested on the obvious pressure in that case.

steps.title: A new question is raised
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question that the scholars asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked of them:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to present a new question, which is stated on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איבעיא להו marks a real open question, not an attack. Here we get only the opening formula; the question itself follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked by them, introducing an open question

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new question after the previous discussion closed
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A new question, stated on the next amud
